evidence.detail: docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:15693 (FR-FLOW-226 Requirement: the skill SHALL record that item's actual dates through the roadmap sync tool ... at the start and at the end of the run) vs docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:17254 (FR-NODE-257 AC-1: Actual Start is proposed only when the computed status is in-progress, done or released) together with docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:17106 (FR-NODE-255 AC-2: in-progress needs a requirement of R in_progress/implemented/verified/blocked, a target of T active, or Actual Start set; otherwise planned). Reachable counterexample in this repository: docs/spec/00.index.md:9 Active Target 5.2.0 and :96 '5.4.0 | version | planned', all 13 requirements of 5.4.0 Status planned. A roadmap item with Targets=5.4.0 computes to `planned` at run start, so the start-of-run sync (FR-FLOW-226 AC-1, :15706) proposes and writes no Actual Start; the end-of-run sync then writes the run-end date as Actual Start. The requirement's own Research note (:15727) acknowledges only the Actual End case.

findings.description: FR-FLOW-226 promises that wave-master records the item's actual start at run start, but under FR-NODE-255 AC-2 and FR-NODE-257 AC-1 an item whose target is planned and whose requirements are planned (the state of 5.4.0 today) computes to planned at run start, so nothing is written then and the end-of-run sync later records the run-end date as Actual Start.
findings.suggested_action: Fix the timing in one place: define the start sync to run after the product target is activated or the first requirement goes in_progress, or give FR-NODE-257 an explicit run-start rule for Actual Start, or narrow FR-FLOW-226's statement and title to what sync can deliver and record the limitation.

evidence.detail: FR-NODE-257 AC-4 applies 'the same ... history-row rules as update' and FR-NODE-256 AC-4 refuses an Actual Start/End change without a reason, while FR-FLOW-226 AC-1 calls sync_roadmap_actuals with apply and item only. Whether AC-4's refusal counts as a 'history-row rule' depends on reading (IR-CLI-115 AC-4 gives sync a --reason option), so no contradiction is proven.

findings.description: Possible missing reason source for sync-written history rows.
